syntheses.title: Use of Mid-Level Representations and Simulation for Autonomous Driving Training
syntheses.body: Both papers B and C emphasize the use of mid-level representations and simulation environments to facilitate autonomous driving training and testing. Paper B describes ChauffeurNet as an RNN that takes mid-level input and outputs driving trajectories, enabling training on real or simulated data and closed-loop simulation testing before real deployment (claims cc49c2d4-b50d-5322-8525-304268249b24, 5fc32090-a96e-5352-b867-05795d95ae56, e4571968-f7ab-5ab9-9db6-21554bbefe13). Paper C presents CARLA as an open-source simulator supporting development, training, and validation of autonomous urban driving systems, providing flexible sensor suite specification and environmental conditions, and enabling controlled scenario evaluation (claims 6dde98eb-ff12-5785-926e-11fbb8cd299b, 2dedfe39-6dab-5024-be2e-997515e0211d, b26241aa-3d3d-560b-9a47-d8c65f50bfa3, 7e8db57a-25dd-55f8-9220-c289a62aea7f, 95c1e45a-f076-5974-87ce-1ddf31a356f5). This theme highlights the shared focus on mid-level input representations and simulation platforms to advance autonomous driving research and deployment.

syntheses.title: End-to-End Learning Approaches for Autonomous Driving
syntheses.body: Papers A and C both discuss end-to-end learning approaches for autonomous driving. Paper A describes a CNN that learns the entire processing pipeline to steer an automobile, generating steering commands from single center camera images (claims e66d15a0-9347-5814-b053-1ff1dea8058d, 82d5df42-8220-51e7-a608-9993016f4e1c, 70eb8202-ac82-55fb-a95a-efb095234403). Paper C uses CARLA to study end-to-end imitation learning among other approaches, supporting training, prototyping, and validation of autonomous driving models including perception and control (claims 34863bb0-827c-5405-a15d-f7229ca8985c, 95c1e45a-f076-5974-87ce-1ddf31a356f5). This theme reflects a shared focus on end-to-end learning methods for autonomous vehicle control.
